run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: In the hotel-reservation namespace the frontend Service routes to a pod that cannot serve its port. Service frontend's selector was changed at 01:36:13 (manager kubectl-patch) from {io.kompose.service: frontend} to {service-route: frontend}, and at 01:36:11-01:36:12 the pod-template label service-route: frontend was added to both the frontend Deployment and the search Deployment (manager OpenAPI-Generator). Only two pods carry service-route: frontend, frontend-5566ddfbfb-ppbtm and search-9cd459687-28pjt, and the frontend Service endpoint list contains both IPs on port 5000 (10.244.234.183 frontend, 10.244.7.218 search), while the search container declares and listens only on 8082 (plus metrics 9092) and registers itself in Consul as 10.244.7.218:8082. Requests addressed to frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 are therefore load-balanced onto a search pod with no listener on 5000. The frontend application itself is not failing: its own spans at 01:36:18-01:36:29 show HTTP GET /hotels and GET /recommendations 200 and HTTP POST /reservation 200 with fast downstream calls and no error-tagged spans, and all 19 namespace pods were Running and Ready with restartCount 0. Because no caller is visible in-cluster or in Jaeger, the refused-request consequence is a strongly supported hypothesis rather than an observed failure rate; that, plus an unverified second candidate (the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate ConfigMaps holding MongoDB admin-privilege revocation scripts whose execution was never observed), is why the conclusion is partial.

claims.text: At 01:36:31 all 19 pods in hotel-reservation were Running and Ready with restartCount 0, including frontend-5566ddfbfb-ppbtm and search-9cd459687-28pjt.

Deployment frontend (hotel-reservation) now has pod-template labels {io.kompose.service: frontend, service-route: frontend}; managedFields show kubectl-client-side-apply at 01:35:57 and an OpenAPI-Generator update at 01:36:11, and the stored last-applied-configuration from 01:35:57 contains only the label io.kompose.service: frontend (no service-route label).

Deployment search (hotel-reservation) now has pod-template labels {io.kompose.service: search, service-route: frontend}; managedFields show kubectl-client-side-apply at 01:35:57 and an OpenAPI-Generator update at 01:36:12, and its last-applied-configuration from 01:35:57 contains only io.kompose.service: search, so the service-route: frontend label was added to the search pod template at 01:36:12.

Service frontend (hotel-reservation) has selector {service-route: frontend}; it was updated by manager kubectl-patch at 01:36:13, and its last-applied configuration from 01:35:57 shows the previous selector {io.kompose.service: frontend} with port 5000 -> targetPort 5000.

The frontend Service endpoint object (observed at 01:38:07, after the window) lists two ready addresses for port 5000: 10.244.234.183 (pod frontend-5566ddfbfb-ppbtm) and 10.244.7.218 (pod search-9cd459687-28pjt).

Only two pods in the cluster carry the label service-route=frontend (frontend-5566ddfbfb-ppbtm and search-9cd459687-28pjt), and the frontend Service is the only Service in the cluster whose selector uses the key service-route.

The search container only declares containerPort 8082 and 9092 (no 5000); ReplicaSet search-9cd459687 confirms these ports, and the search pod log states 'Read target port: 8082' and registers 'srv-search' at 10.244.7.218:8082.

The frontend application itself was serving successfully in the last seconds of the window: frontend spans at 01:36:29 show HTTP GET /hotels 200 (3034 us) and HTTP GET /recommendations 200 (2208-2489 us), and POST /reservation spans at 01:36:18-01:36:28 show http.status_code=200 (6.1-12.4 ms) with downstream /reservation.Reservation/MakeReservation, /user.User/CheckUser, /search.Search/Nearby, /rate.Rate/GetRates, /geo.Geo/Nearby and /profile.Profile/GetProfiles spans and zero error-tagged rows.

Blackbox probe probe_success{instance="frontend.hotel-reservation:5000",job="blackbox-hotel-reservation"} read 0 at every 15 s sample from 01:34:30 to 01:36:15 and 1 at 01:36:30; the series starts at 01:34:30 while the pods were only created at 01:35:57-01:36:13, so the early zeros coincide with startup and only the 01:36:15 zero falls after the frontend pod was serving.

Because the frontend Service has two endpoints on port 5000 and one of them (search pod 10.244.7.218) has no listener on 5000, a share of the client requests sent to frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 are DNATed to a closed port and fail (connection refused) while requests landing on 10.244.234.183:5000 succeed; this explains intermittent frontend failures with no error span, since a refused connection never produces a frontend span. The exact failure share was not measured.

Two ConfigMaps in hotel-reservation, failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate, hold fault scripts revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh and revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh that connect as admin/admin and call db.revokeRolesFromUser(...,[{role:'readWrite',db:'geo-db'|'rate-db'}]), plus remove-admin-mongo.sh and mitigation scripts.

The MongoDB privilege-revocation settings were not shown to be in effect: mongodb-rate logged Authentication succeeded for principal admin (SCRAM-SHA-1) at 01:36:05, 01:36:12 and 01:36:20 and created collection rate-db.inventory at 01:36:05, and mongodb-geo logged admin authentication and createCollection geo-db.geo at 01:36:06; rate and geo gRPC calls also returned normally at 01:36:29.

A second, still unverified candidate cause is that the revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh or revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh scripts from ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo or failure-admin-rate were executed after 01:36:20, which would make geo or rate fail later DB reads/writes with MongoDB authorization errors even though authentication still succeeds; no execution of those scripts and no 'not authorized' log line was observed in the window.

Pod-level damage (crash, OOMKill, eviction, resource-limit exhaustion in the namespace) is rejected as the cause: every hotel-reservation pod was Running and Ready with restartCount 0 at 01:36:31, the only namespace events are Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started/Killing/SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete and a FailedScheduling against an already-deleted pod from the initial rollout, and there are no NetworkPolicies in the namespace that could explain refused connections.

Remove the label service-route: frontend from the pod template of Deployment search (or restore Service frontend's selector to io.kompose.service: frontend) so the frontend Service selects only the frontend pod, then confirm the frontend endpoint list contains a single address on port 5000 and that external requests stop being refused.

gaps: No caller or load generator exists in the cluster (no load-generator pod/Job/Deployment, not in Jaeger's service list), so the request failure rate at frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 that the misrouted endpoint should cause could not be measured; traces contain only requests that reached the frontend pod.

The change_history integration is not available, so who or what operates managers 'OpenAPI-Generator' (Deployment patches at 01:36:11/01:36:12) and 'kubectl-patch' (Service patch at 01:36:13), and the exact patch bodies, are unknown; only manager names and timestamps are recorded.

The app and observability stack were created 01:35:57-01:36:13, so there is no pre-change baseline: Jaeger traces exist only from 01:36:18 onward, Loki namespace logs only from about 01:35:57, and the probe_success series starts 01:34:30 and is dominated by startup failures.

kube-state-metrics endpoint series were internally inconsistent at 01:36:30 (frontend endpoint address 10.244.7.249; kube_endpoint_address_available 0 for endpoints search, user and all mongodb-*), so those readings were not used to describe the endpoint set; the live Endpoints object was used instead and was only observable after the window.

Queries that returned no data (no_data status, therefore not evidence of absence): get_series for traces_span_metrics_calls_total (no span-metric series exist), traces_search_by_tags service=frontend tag error=true and service=frontend min_duration 500ms (nothing matched), Loki selector {namespace="hotel-reservation"} |~ "(?i)unauthorized|not authorized|access denied" (no line matched) and the same selector for the window ending 01:35:00 (no lines), and kube_pod_container_status_terminated_reason for hotel-reservation (no series).

Whether the failure-admin-geo / failure-admin-rate ConfigMap scripts were ever executed is unknown (no executor pod/Job, no 'not authorized' log line, and MongoDB user/role state cannot be read with the available tools), so that candidate remains open.

The trace view is a biased sample of roughly one second of traffic (01:36:18-01:36:29) with no complete trace graph, so absence of error spans there does not prove the Service never refuses connections.
next_steps: Apply the label fix on Deployment search (or revert the frontend Service selector) and re-check the frontend Endpoints object for a single port-5000 address.
Observe the actual client side (load generator or ingress logs) for connection-refused/5xx to frontend.hotel-reservation:5000 before and after the fix to quantify the failure share.
If the MongoDB fault library is intended to be active, verify the readWrite role of user admin on geo-db and rate-db, and watch the geo and rate application logs for MongoDB authorization errors.

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

data.remove-admin-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

echo "Removing admin user..."

mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.dropUser('admin');"

echo "Admin user removed successfully"
data.revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
# TARGET_DB="rate-db"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Downgrading admin user privileges..."

# Connect to MongoDB and revoke roles
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.revokeRolesFromUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: 'readWrite', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges downgraded"
data.remove-mitigate-admin-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

# Connect to MongoDB and create the admin user
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Admin user recreated"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"

     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privilege restored successfully"

#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
